result.title: CausalEvo: Causal Skill Self-Evolution for Health LLM Agents
result.comment: GenAI for Health Workshop @ NeurIPS 2026, Sydney
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents for health can accumulate reusable textual skills from task feedback, such as calculation criteria, measurement time points, and formula units. Deciding which skills to retain is consequential: useful rules improve later answers, while faulty generalizations propagate errors. We propose CausalEvo, a method for causal skill self-evolution that estimates the relative effects of deliberately changed skill sets while holding the model weights, feedback cases, and rule count fixed. At each evolution step, a frozen LLM proposes candidate rules, which are pooled with the incumbent skills so that the current skill set remains a feasible choice. Paired skill replacements against shared background rules are scored on the same feedback cases; least squares converts the score differences into relative skill values, and the top-ranked rules are retained, favoring incumbents on ties. A decision-loss bound separates candidate support, approximation, and estimation errors. On six MedCalc-Bench-Verified tasks with 120 held-out cases, CausalEvo achieves 60.00% accuracy, compared with 55.83% for SkillOpt and 51.67% without skills. Across the recorded training configurations, which use different optimization budgets, it consumes 55.6% fewer training tokens than SkillOpt. Gains concentrate in particular calculations alongside regressions on others, and paired accuracy intervals include zero. CausalEvo turns task feedback into controlled decisions about skill retention and replacement. Project repository: https://github.com/txbrook/CausalEvo

AI.brief_summary: CausalEvo 面向健康 LLM 智能体的文本技能自演化：冻结模型提出候选规则，与已有技能池配对替换，在同一反馈案例上打分并用最小二乘转化为相对技能价值，据此决定保留或替换哪些规则。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「配对替换＋最小二乘估计相对贡献」的因果式技能取舍线索，可能可供核查 latent 推理步骤或状态更新的贡献分配与监督问题；但该工作处理健康领域纯文本技能，与视觉状态生成、证据使用无直接联系，是否可迁移需较多核查。
